classification.difficultyReason: Interpret whether each stated rise or fall gives1+p or1−p, recover the earlier amount by division, and apply the requested nearest10 rounding. Familiar linked percentage operations, including a rise over100%.

content.prompt: A research institute is trying to find out how much water Lake Grendel had 1000 years ago. The lake now contains 24 000 megalitres, but there are various conflicting theories about the percentage change over the last 1000 years. Find how much water the lake had 1000 years ago, correct to the nearest 10 megalitres, if in the last 1000 years the volume has:

answer.worked:
The present volume is $180\%$ of the original.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=24000\div1.80\\\text{Original volume}&=\frac{40000}{3}\text{ ML}\\\text{Original volume}&\approx13330\text{ ML}\end{align*}$$
Rounded to the nearest 10 megalitres.

The present volume is $72\%$ of the original.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=24000\div0.72\\\text{Original volume}&=\frac{100000}{3}\text{ ML}\\\text{Original volume}&\approx33330\text{ ML}\end{align*}$$
Rounded to the nearest 10 megalitres.

The present volume is $240\%$ of the original.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=24000\div2.40\\\text{Original volume}&=10000\text{ ML}\end{align*}$$

The present volume is $96\%$ of the original.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=24000\div0.96\\\text{Original volume}&=25000\text{ ML}\end{align*}$$
